title: Cross-surface Pattern Bridge and Figma Interoperability for Cost & Rollout Canvas
creator: Marina Chen
description: Problem: Multiple console surfaces (Cost Explorer, Rollout Inspector, Metrics Dashboards) are drifting in component usage and token naming. This causes inconsistent spacing, button affordances, and chart legend behavior across routes. Goal: create a pattern bridge (canonical components + usage examples) and a Figma interoperability layer so designers and engineers can consume the same tokens, variants, and component guidelines across Cost & Rollout canvases. Deliverables: 1) Figma library with canonical components and published token file; 2) migration guide for existing dashboard and rollout screens; 3) a lightweight spec for engineers describing variant props and accessibility expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical Figma library published and versioned (v1) with tokens file exported
Token naming map created mapping old token names to canonical names
Three example screens (Cost Explorer list, Rollout Inspector timeline, Metrics sparklines) implemented as Figma instances demonstrating variants
Dev spec doc with prop mappings and 2 example React component usages reviewed by frontend eng
Design QA checklist defined and applied to one pilot rollout route
No visual regressions on pilot route after migration (per snapshot test and designer signoff)

decisions: Adopt semantic token names (surface-bg, surface-elev-1, accent-primary) instead of raw color tokens to reduce per-surface variants
Use Figma Variables as single source of truth and publish a versioned export to the design-assets bucket
Prefer smaller component surface footprint (compound components made from primitives) so engineers can tree-shake unused variants

Legacy dashboard snapshot tests rely on old token names; test update window needs coordination with QA
Need alignment on spacing scale (8px vs 10px base) — frontend prefers 8px, some design mocks use 10px spacing
